title: Cardinal Billing Account Pay Plan, Payment Method and Due Day Changes: Questions Answered
content:
**Rule.** The pay plan of a Cardinal Billing Account may be changed during the term only where the current plan allows a midterm plan change, and only while the account status is current; a pay plan or due-day change is processed only while the account status is current. On a midterm change, the unbilled premium of the term is re-spread over the new plan's remaining installments from the change date; amounts already billed stay due as billed and no fee is charged for the change. The new plan's autopay requirement and accepted payment methods must be satisfied by the method on file. A policy carrying a financial-responsibility filing may use a plan only where that plan allows such a policy. The installment due day may move to any day from the 1st through the 28th of the month, by no more than the pay plan's largest due-day move in one change and no more than the pay plan's due-day changes allowed in a term. A change of payment method or autopay enrollment takes effect from the next invoice not yet issued. Plan, method and due-day changes are not available while a certified-funds restriction would be broken by the new method.

## Questions the rule answers

**In what account status can a plan or due-day change be processed?**
Only current. The status is read from the company's record of the billing account before the change. An account in notice pending, cancelled for nonpayment, collections or closed status is not current.

**What happens to installments already billed when the plan changes midterm?**
They stay due as billed. Only the unbilled premium of the term is re-spread over the new plan's remaining installments from the change date. No fee is charged for the change.

**Which due days are possible?**
Any day from the 1st through the 28th. The 29th, 30th and 31st are outside that range.

**When does a new payment method or autopay setting take effect?**
From the next invoice not yet issued; an invoice already issued is not affected.

**Can a customer under a certified-funds restriction switch to a method that is not certified funds?**
No. Plan, method and due-day changes are not available while the restriction would be broken by the new method.

**Can a policy with an SR-22 or FR-44 filing move to any plan?**
Only to a plan that allows a policy carrying a financial-responsibility filing.

## Due-day moves (hypothetical plan allowing a 10-day move and one change per term)

| Current due day | Requested due day | Move | Within the rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12th | 22nd | 10 days | Yes |
| 12th | 23rd | 11 days | No |
| 20th | 30th | 10 days | No, the 30th is outside the 1st through 28th |
